utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's examination-in-chief continuing. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: As we have started now, we'll have our break at 11.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, do I understand it's half an hour break at 11.35 or 20 minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It will be 20 minutes, because we have lost a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Pantelic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Wednesday we started analysing some evidence, and now we are going to continue with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Registrar, please could we have Exhibit D4/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, what can you say about this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Vox" is a newspaper, a periodical that was published in Sarajevo, that was distributed publicly. One day in Samac this page happened to be on the walls of houses, on chestnut trees by the pedestrian paths. This is a very morbid paper that instigated violation, retaliation, aggression in the harshest possible terms. I recognise here the heads of some well-known politicians of that time. The first head is the head of Mr. Radovan Karadzic; then Koljevic; then Slobodan Milosevic; and then Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was your impression, your personal impression regarding this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This caused fear, fear, fear for one's own life, being a Serb who lived in that town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D21/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you take a look on the right-hand side. Let it stay on the ELMO, but perhaps you can see it better on the right-hand side rather than on the monitor itself. What can you say about this document, Mr. Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of this document. This appeared also on the facades of buildings, on the chestnut trees by the pedestrian paths. I know a few names here. Most of them were Muslims. As far as I can see, all of them were Muslims that had a pro-Yugoslav orientation, who were loyal to the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the JNA as the only legal armed force. However, they were under the attack of the newly-established paramilitary formations of the Muslims. In a way this called for lynching them, for condemning them, eliminating them. This was the message.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He can indicate that's what -- his impression is that, but that's not what it says here. That's not what the exhibit says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Ninkovic. What were comments regarding this document like in town?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an event that was discussed for days. It caused major polemics, friction, clashes, and it caused unrest among the public in Samac and led to an escalation of inter-ethnic tensions, and also within the Muslim community itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to discuss this list with any one of the persons on the list, how such a person experienced the fact that he or she was put on this list? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I can't remember having discussed it with any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D -- sorry, D28/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, what can you say about this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't seen this document before, but I can say that the Public Security Station of Samac is in charge of taking measures regarding the movement of vehicles and persons. So I believe that this document, or rather, this order was issued in that sense. I mean, I think that is the way it is. It's not that I'm assuming it. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this order being carried out, this order issued by the police in Samac? Because this has to do with a curfew, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the inhabitants observe this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was issued on the 17th of April. As far as I know, on that day in Samac there was fighting, so there was an armed clash. So on the basis of that, one may infer that not everybody observed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. To the best of your knowledge, how long was this order in force? In May, June, and later as well?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was in force until conditions were created to have it withdrawn. I don't know whether it was two or three days or something like that. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, there's something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Excuse me. There's a matter in the transcript that's not clear. Mr. Pantelic asked in reference to this document: "Was this order being carried out, this order issued by the police in Samac?" And then he went on to ask a second question: "Because this has to do with a curfew, doesn't it?" Answer: "Yes." I take it that from the subsequent answers of the witness that he probably meant that the order was in fact issued, but it's not clear if he's saying yes, it's got something to do with a curfew, or yes, the order was issued. And I want to know whether this order was issued and acted upon, if the witness is now testifying about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you have any knowledge about whether this document was actually issued.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, but that doesn't really answer Mr. Di Fazio's point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: It was issued, but was it actually carried out. I think that was Mr. Di Fazio's point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And that was exactly my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because I notice that it's -- it was in my previous one, the second part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My next question, although you've already answered, but just in case: Was this actually being enforced?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out about that at the police checkpoint that was placed on the outskirts of town, before one entered town. I think it was being enforced because there were police checkpoints at the entrance into town. However, as I've already said, on the 17th in town there was fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D35/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take a look at this document; it has several pages. Please familiarise yourself with it. Take a look at it. Leaf through it. What can you say about this document, Mr. Ninkovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let me have a look at it. On this document I see a list of persons who were issued weapons. The type of weapon is listed, the quantity of ammunition, the number of clips, so it looks as if it were a unit that has such-and-such weapons, such-and-such amounts of ammunition, et cetera. I personally know some of the persons here. I know Mr. Sulejman Tihic. I know Mr. Izet Izetbegovic. They held the highest positions in the Party of Democratic Action in Samac at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any non-Muslims on this list?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. No, it's only Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at page 3 of this document and give me your comments. What is this all about? What is this specification?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the upper part of the third page, we have infantry weapons, automatic -- automatic -- there is ammunition 7.62, that is used for automatic rifles like Kalashnikovs. Several types of ammunition. Some is incendiary, others is not. There are tracer bullets and others. Then on page 3, under 4 and 5 it says "long and short." I assume that this is ammunition for pistols, because 9 millimetre calibres have long and short bullets. That's a well-known thing. Then in the lower part of page 3, there are rifle grenade projectiles that are used for destroying protected trenches and the like, fortifications as well. I can see explosives here as well, detonators and so on. So this is explosives and other necessary weapons for destroying larger fortified buildings or also bridges and the like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity of discussing this document with someone in Samac and did anybody mention this document, what its purpose was and organisation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D37/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can you tell us about this document, please?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was issued in the Republic of Croatia. In the letterhead I can see "the Republic of Croatia," and "the Crisis Staff of Slavonski Brod Municipality." This is on the river Sava in the Republic of Croatia, some 40 kilometres away from Bosanski Samac, and this is a certificate in the name of Alija Fitozovic. He is an inhabitant of Bosanski Samac whom I know. We went to secondary school together. When I was in the first grade, he was in the fourth grade of the technical school in Bosanski Samac and that's how I know him. I can also see here the stamp of the organs of the Republic of Croatia, more specifically, the Municipal Assembly of Slavonski Brod. I can also see here the signature of the president of the Crisis Staff, whose name is Pilipovic and whom I don't know, obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read this signature more carefully, the second name. What is typed here? What family name is typed on the document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is Franjo Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. The last name on my document -- can you spell the last name, if you could.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: F-r-n-o -- Fiplovic. I apologise. My eyesight is not that good. So this is a document, a certificate which allowed Alija Fitozovic to cross the river Sava every day and go to Slavonski Brod to perform certain duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is handwritten below "Slavonski Brod"?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says Slavonski Samac?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Slavonski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavonski Samac is across the River Sava opposite Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the 29th of December -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: This last passage of questioning has not revealed anything that we could not have seen by simply looking at the document ourselves. I know Your Honours are concerned about time. We're being asked to read out, being asked to look at who -- the date of the document, the person who signed the document. Well, you just need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: He can tell you. All this information that this witness is being kept here to give us is material that we can get from the face of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Of the document, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Now, the if this witness knows something about this document or knows something about the activities of Alija Fitozovic or the background to the creation or the reason for the existence of this document, all well and good, but -- the Prosecution will listen avidly. But this examination-in-chief is giving us nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you reorganise your examination-in-chief, because once an exhibit is admitted into evidence, then all the contents are on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just have a couple of issues to clarify with this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, in the second paragraph of this certificate some checkpoints are mentioned on the bridges in Slavonski Brod and in Slavonski Samac. Can you please tell me what you know about these checkpoints, who organised them, who manned those checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the big bridge on the Sava, between Bosanski Samac and Slavonski Samac, which is in Croatia, there were two checkpoints. On the Bosnian side there was the checkpoint manned by the reserve police of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is, of the Samac MUP. And on the other bank there was a checkpoint manned by the Croatian MUP. So nobody could cross the bridge without being controlled, and this gentleman, Alija Fitozovic, had a document allowing him passage from one side to another through the checkpoints and that was a certain privilege at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your personal knowledge of the activities of Alija Fitozovic in December 1991 through April 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija Fitozovic at that time was well known to the general public in Samac as a prominent member of the SDA who was in charge of establishing paramilitary Muslim formations in Samac. He was very close to the military circles in Croatia, and he always travelled between Bosanski Samac, the SDA, and the HDZ, and the military circles in Croatia. It is also a well-known fact that he was in charge of establishing and commanding the Muslim paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since your job pertained to the area of defence and administrative procedures, can you please tell us what was his professional military background did he have. Had he undergone a special military training or did he have any other knowledge, military knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, he did have some training, military training and training regarding the compulsory military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have Exhibit D38/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can you tell us about this document, Mr. Ninkovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can see here is the list of automatic rifles, Kalashnikovs, AK-47, made in Russia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Pantelic, you're going through the same thing Mr. -- the Prosecution objected to, describing what is in the document, which is already on record.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, did you ever see this document before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit D39/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please also look at the second page of this document and tell us what you can about this document.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are military formations, i.e., groups in charge of certain tasks and duties. As far as I can see, members are all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are they from?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're all from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about such groups?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know it was well known that there was a paramilitary Muslim formation in Samac and that they had different groups for communications, intelligence, reconnaissance, sabotage groups, and they have all the other groups that normally are on the strength of any army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you -- how did you learn about these groups and about their checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had contacts with some Muslims who were of pro-Yugoslav orientation and who spoke to me about those things they mentioned some names, and I also know some of the people on this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you know? Just a few names. Can you mention a few names.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. Hakija Srna, Edin Nurkic, Avdo Piric, Mensur Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D41/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, tell me, do you have any personal knowledge of the existence of checkpoints and certain groups consisting of Muslims from Samac? And I am particularly interested in the period of March and April 1992.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the period during which the paramilitary formations were already well organised and they started carrying out their actions. They put up their checkpoints. They were armed. They had records. They also enlarged their strength by mobilising new men, and this period was full of events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally know about these groups and the checkpoints that they manned?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew personally of these checkpoints, and I was personally harassed on one of the checkpoints on the bridge between Prud and Samac closer to Samac. They were armed. They carried semi-automatic and automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see this document before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when you see the marks for the checkpoints 1 and 2, where are these checkpoints in Samac, these two places that are mentioned in the document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the main checkpoints at the entrance to Samac, close to the veterinary clinic; and the second checkpoint was on the other entrance to Samac, on the direction coming from Modrica, close to the hospital and the Mebos company. These were the main checkpoints, and they were facing Serbian villages. Let me just tell you who was in charge of the -- whoever was in charge of those checkpoints held the key position in the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally witness some activities regarding the armament of these people?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My office was at Secretariat of National Defence. This is a building in the centre of town. On the ground floor is the bank and on the first floor is the Secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- Those who held checkpoints held the key position in the defence of the town. Here it's page 13 in my laptop. Probably -- line 1 and 2. Actually, what he said -- he said -- what I heard that he said is that the one who controlled these checkpoints actually controlled the town. And if my colleague Pantelic could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe he can -- yes. Mr. Pantelic, can you clarify with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I will -- I will. Thank you, my colleague, for this intervention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat for the record your. Your last sentence was about the checkpoints. And you said that whoever controlled these checkpoints, and so on. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever controlled these two checkpoints by the veterinary clinic and by the hospital and the Mebos company practically or effectively controlled the town, the main entrances to the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You started talking about your office which was in the municipal secretariat in the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What period are we talking about? When was that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in late March, early April. I and my colleague --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which year was that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in 1992. We were sitting in my office and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please give us his name.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Arandjic. Across the road from our building there are a little park, and in its corner there was the Islam community. We saw a car. It was an Opel Kadett and there were also two men who were unloading some boxes, some crates. We stepped out to observe. We found it suspicious that somebody would be unloading some crates in front of the Islam community. These crates were of olive colour, and we suspected that they contained infantry weapons. When we came closer we saw that they were taking out the last box and we saw that it bore the JNA insignia. So it was indeed a box for infantry weapons. These were also the premises of the SDA for Samac municipality. When we saw that, we returned. We called the police and informed them about all that. The police told us that they would send a patrol to investigate; however, later on when we contacted the police again, they told us that the patrol had already been there and left and that the car had gone through the MUP checkpoint in Grebnice, on the road to Orasje, on the road between Samac and Orasje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me, in the time period December 1991/April 1992, what do you know about certain cases? Were there any cases of confiscation of illegal weapons? And if so, please give us details. We know that that bridge was a highly-frequented bridge.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time there was a checkpoint in Pisari, which is a town in the direction of Modrica. On the road between Samac and Modrica, there was a checkpoint of the JNA military police there. And when conducting a routine control of a bus, they found weaponry, ammunition, and small infantry weapons. They also found a knife or a machete, something like that looked like a machete. It was hand-made and it had the words "Srbosjek" engraved in it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note Srbosjek --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does "Srbosjek" stand for?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that it was a blade intended to slaughter Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether in Samac there was any other information circulated regarding weaponry and possible confiscation of it. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please. If Your Honours please, if I may assist the Tribunal. I'm not objecting, but that last answer is just meaningless. What you've got is an allegation from the witness who may know more about it - I don't know - but he says that on the road between Samac and Modrica weaponry was found and this machete with the words on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Now, you don't know who had the weaponry. You don't know who seized the weaponry other than the fact that it was JNA. You don't know what the weaponry was. It's just a slab of information that you will never be able to use effectively. If I may assist Mr. Pantelic, he may care to get the point out of the evidence and it will also save on my cross-examination time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm very grateful to my learned friend, but he's a little bit running ahead. Because several of my next questions, I will just make a final question -- not to split them, you know, many times but what is his personal knowledge about the sides involved in these operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a matter of efficiency.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I give some more details regarding that event?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that won't be necessary.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether you knew about any other events in Samac from December 1991 until April 1992. Were there any other events involving confiscation of illegal weaponry?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time Croats from Bosnia-Herzegovina went as volunteers to assist the armed formations of Croatia which were at war with the Yugoslav People's Army. They frequently went there in buses, in shifts, especially from Western Herzegovina. I know the road map in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The main communication was Zenica, Sarajevo, Doboj, and this bridge over Sava River, which led to Croatia. The military police stopped the buses and found on the buses people that had been at the front line. They had certain documents on them, weapons such as small arms, pistols, hand grenades, cold weapons from the front, as I've mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me, that period of time, December 1991/April 1992, the events that you've just described to us, what ethnic group was involved in that process of illegal weapons smuggling and arming, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please could we have Exhibit D42/1, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, this is document D42/1 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's ID, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, please tell me, what do you know about this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a so-called block scheme or organigram which in the military depicts the organisational chart of units. We can see here at the top the political organ that was called the Crisis Staff, and then underneath it we have a developed military structure. We have a military staff and then underneath, various units. We have units in different branches of service, such as sabotage units, communication units, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is written in the right corner, the section that has to do with the staff, with the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a political organ which was directly appointed by a political party. That's the only explanation that makes sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This type of chart, was it typically made at the time when you held positions in the Secretariat for People's Defence? Does it correspond to the doctrine that was in force when you held the position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you're asking me about a professional -- as a professional, then I will tell you that in a military formation you never have a political organ that is directly superior to it and can issue commands to the military units. It is a very unusual link depicted here, the one between the military staff and the municipal staff. There were no such cases in the doctrine and organisational structure of the JNA, and this is not known in the military doctrine at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document during preparations for my testimony here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I meant before, prior to coming to The Hague. I'm talking to the time period prior to coming here.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milos Savic is a lawyer who worked at the Public Security Station in Samac and who was in charge of criminal proceedings. Rather, he filed charges against people who had illegal weapons in Samac. He showed me a number of documents, including this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1992. Let's say June or July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what context did Milos Savic mention this and other documents? Can you describe to us what other documents were. What did he show to you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milos Savic is a judge in Samac now, so he now deals with proceedings against people who possessed weapons. He showed me --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- Intervene at the moment. This is not what the witness said. So he now deals with proceedings against people. He was talking about that time, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us go back to the beginning, because we have a problem with the transcript. You started telling us how Milos Savic was a judge.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Milos Savic is a judge now. But at that time, he was a criminal detective in the Public Security Station in Samac and he was involved in filing charges against people on whom weapons had been found and he dealt with documents depicting paramilitary formations in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he mention to you any names of people against whom charges were filed? Who were the suspects in that case?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tihic Sulejman, Izet Izetbegovic, Alija Fitozovic, Namik Suljic, and some other people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that he mentioned some other documents to you too. Can you tell us what other documents dealt with.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He showed me some documents that were plans. Some were handwritten. Some were typewritten. And these documents illustrated that there had been paramilitary units. It described the structure, the personnel of that unit, the weaponry that they had, and it also described a direct link between the SDA, because a lot of documents had the SDA heading, letterhead, or the SDA seal, the SDA from Samac. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I don't object to this -- to the previous question, but I think for you -- in order to understand the evidence of this witness, it's probably important that he clarify for us what he means by "paramilitary units." He's used the term throughout his evidence. For example, he used it in reference to the document which showed patrols and referred -- Muslim patrols, or SDA patrols, and he use add reference -- he used the word "paramilitary" in describing those patrols. Now, the word conjures up different things in different people's minds, and it's important that we are all clear about what precisely he means by "paramilitary formations." Does he mean groups of armed -- officially groups of armed men sent in by the authorities from Bosnia and Herzegovina, or is he referring purely and simply to formations within the political parties? It's just not very clear to me when he uses the word if he's just referring to small isolated groups or large well-organised formations within the SDA. He may have a particular understanding, and it's probably important, since he uses the word from time to time, for him to give us a clearer idea. I suggest that would be useful for you in order to understand -- understand his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I think this was a very appropriate intervention, both for the sake of those who are laymen here and for the Trial Chamber. Please explain what you understand under the term "paramilitary formation" and then I will ask you something else regarding your personal knowledge from Samac. Please tell us what you as a professional understand under the term "paramilitary formation."

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are speaking on the base of the law, the only legal armed formation or structure was the Yugoslav People's Army. That means that all other armed formations that are party-based or party-affiliated, regardless of the number of their personnel and weaponry, are considered paramilitary formations. We can say that a group consisting of three members is a paramilitary formation, just like one that has 500 members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question has to do with Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is that -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. That's precisely clarified exactly what I was concerned about. So it's anything from 3 to 500 in this witness's testimony. Now I understand his evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ninkovic. Now, please tell me this: When you spoke to people who were policemen, investigative organs, and also based on your personal knowledge prior to April 1992, what were your conclusions, if any, regarding the existence of paramilitary formations in the town of Samac itself and the municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my testimony so far, one can conclude that I have clearly stated my position that there had been paramilitary formations in Samac consisting of Muslims who had been armed through various illegal channels and that these activities had been coordinated by the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge regarding the Croat ethnic community in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that the ethnic composition of the population in town was dominated by Croats and Muslims. There were fewer --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: By Serbs and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were fewer Croats. The Croats mostly resided in Prud, Domaljevac, Bazik, and Grebnice. I as an official of the Secretariat for People's Defence can say that in these parts of municipalities, the paramilitary formations were established earlier than in the town itself, because in Samac we had the Croatian Democratic Union, which was the first of the national parties to be established prior to the SDS and the SDA, and it had very close links to the HDZ in Croatia. They had political consultation between them. They took over terms, concepts, and platform, and they established their paramilitary formations prior to April of 1992. An especially important stronghold was Domaljevac, Bazik, Grebnice. Back in 1990 when we sent out call-ups for military conscripts, we had cases where mailmen did not dare go to those Croatian villages because they were afraid. The mailmen therefore had difficulties in delivering mail in that area back in 1990. That means that at that time the obstruction of the Federal army had started.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender into evidence this document that we have discussed, D42/1, because that was an ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any objection? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I -- yes. I think there is an objection. In fact, I think Mr. Weiner should address you on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: It was a document that I think was tendered through Fitozovic and Mr. Weiner handled that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the issue all along has been authenticity of portions of this document. This witness hasn't added anything. Alija Fitozovic explained what the document was, that it was part of a hierarchy of a military group, the TO that he was developing, and that certain portions were added to this by -- or forged on this or falsely added to this, and this witness here was -- has not testified that he was present when this document was drafted, that he has any information concerning the drafting. He didn't even see this document until June or July. This document was drafted -- the original, wherever that is, was drafted sometime in early to mid-April, and then portions of this, according to Alija -- the testimony of Alija Fitozovic was forged on top of this, to make this a false document and to use it as some sort of propaganda tool. This witness hasn't added anything, so we're still at the same place that we were several months ago. We still have a document which has forged sections. And unless this witness can testify as to its authenticity, there is nothing this witness has added.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a little bit absolutely and strange. This witness is not speaking whether the author of this document is Alija Fitozovic. He simply speaks about the document that he saw from the detective, police officer, Mr. Milos Savic. And then as we did in all other cases with the tendering of documents, we did it like a normal way. If my learned friend has some problems with regard to the authenticity, et cetera, he may -- he may call for some kind of examination or stuff like that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic. The point is clear. The Prosecution is still objecting on grounds of authenticity. So it's not similar to how the other exhibits have been admitted. It's totally different. Authenticity is being contested by the Prosecution, and unless you call evidence to show or you call the person -- the maker of that document or the people who were present when that document was being made.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Or maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: To -- to satisfy the Prosecution on authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I must proceed with the additional forensic analysis. So my handwriting expert should deal with that. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. The Defence can deal with authenticity in the way they think best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it still remains an ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In that case, I will submit this document to our handwriting expert, and he will give his opinion. Thank you, Your Honour. Now could we have document -- it's Exhibit, in fact, I believe, yes, D43/1, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If you go back to the transcript, you'll find that in July it was discussed again and it remained ID, and one would have thought that since that time you would have already got your handwriting expert to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: With this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You should just check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at the document carefully, please. The copy is not very good. This has been provided to us by the Prosecution in the bundle of their evidence.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you can take the document -- maybe you'll find it easier to read it. Mr. Ninkovic, what can you tell us about this document, i.e., this piece of evidence?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another plan which carries a specific weight. This document was compiled by a minimum of two persons, if not more. Why do I say that? Firstly, let me tell you about the group or the team which worked on compiling this document. This team consists of some people from the political life or an individual who may have been a member of a municipal organ, maybe a municipal board who was privy to the complete information regarding the positions of that political organisation. And also, there was somebody on the team who had experience and knowledge in the area of military profession. Also, people involved in the drafting of this document were people from the area of economy and finance. So it must have been a very competent team who drafted this document very professionally, and for that reason I believe that this document carries special weight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What institution are we talking about? What does this document serve?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document serves to establish the territorial political community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the very beginning of the document, can you please read the thesis for compiling the plan of what.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you infer, based on this document? You mentioned a party organisation more specifically. Which party was that? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I object to any inferences being drawn, unless the basis for this -- this portion of the testimony is made clear. I've got no objection to the witness telling us what this document is about or who made it, why it was made, and so on and so forth. But what is not clear at this stage is the basis upon which he is saying all of this. Normally, one would expect Mr. Pantelic to have asked him if he had seen the document before, if he was familiar with its contents, with its creation, and the reasons for its creation, and so on, and then go on to ask these questions. But that basis hasn't been laid yet. All you've got is the witness telling us his conclusions and we have absolutely no idea on what basis he is giving this evidence. And so therefore if Mr. Pantelic wants to lead this, we should ascertain on what basis the witness is making these assertions about the nature of the document, the content of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The basis is -- MR. DI FAZIO: And so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the basis is very simple: We have a professional here who can give us additional information about the document and the form by itself. That's the first point. Because up to now, we didn't -- we were not able here during the Prosecution case for various reasons - I don't know - but simply during the Defence case it's obvious, we didn't have a person, professional educated with these particular issues to give us explanation first of all what does this document says. And then during the examination of this witness, we shall come to the following points: Which political party was mentioned in this document, what names from the Municipality of Samac were mentioned in this document, and finally that will be a basis for the evidence of this witness, because he, we know, is a professional for the matters of defence. And I cannot ask all these questions to a physician or to the engineer or whoever. I mean, we have the right person, I believe, here to hear his testimony. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I thought that was the basis on which the questions were being asked, and on that basis I object to this portion of the testimony. The document is -- if you look at it, it covers all sorts of activities, all sorts of areas. And it seems to me that this witness is in no better position than ourselves to be able to look at it and read and understand the plain intent and meaning of the words. The words speak for themselves. It's very clear. If the witness could tell us something about the creation of this document, how it was made, why it was made, the intent and purpose behind it, all well and good. I would have no objection. He can't do that. All he can tell us is what's written here, and we can read that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think there's a problem here, Mr. Pantelic, because this witness has come here as a fact witness. He is not an expert in the sense that you have put it, vis-a-vis his knowledge of this document, because he was not there when it was created.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, that's correct. But we have certain -- well, we have certain bases to think that this was created by the Croatian party in Samac, that this was created within the municipality of Samac, and the members of the HDZ in Samac - because clearly there are some signs and there are some details here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He is a fact witness, Your Honour. I will simply ask him: Do you know what the name is here? Do you know this man? What was his position and what are your conclusions or personal knowledge about his activities? And then that will be the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. That is fine. MR. DI FAZIO: That's fine. I've got no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If that is the line of question, that's fine. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, tell me, please, can you infer from this document -- or maybe you know from some other source which party organisation is here in question.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know two people on this list. I was in personal contact with them on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What names are these?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mato Madzarevic from Domaljevac who worked in Samac municipality. He was a member of the executive council in charge of communal affairs. And Mato Milovic [as interpreted], the president of the municipality of Isevo [phoen] -- I apologise. So the second person is Mato Nujic, the president of the Samac Municipal Assembly, highly positioned in the hierarchy of the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, what is your conclusion about this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we please comment on this document, just briefly, if I may, the way the document was drafted and compiled?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I base my observations regarding this document on the regulations in the areas of planning which existed in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. These are plans for the establishment of defence civilian structures. In those regulations, there is a very clear indication on what elements should a document contain. And in this document -- this document tells me that somebody who was familiar with these regulations was involved in drafting these documents. So somebody who had experience in these -- in this area, because I was also involved in that area. This, I can tell based on the thesis which are very precise and elaborated in great detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, did you ever see this document before? If you did, when was that? If not, can you tell us that you didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Still 10 minutes, yes, for -- we are working -- because I'm a little bit lost because of this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I said 11.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 11.45. Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Thank you so much. Thank you, Mr. Usher, please. Could we have now Exhibit D56/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at the document, Mr. Ninkovic. What could you tell us about this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was issued by the Department of Defence in Samac. It was signed by the person whom I know personally, Srecko Handzic [phoen]. So the document is authentic, and it is a customary document certifying to some facts about the person who is on military records, and this is a certificate that Simic Blagoje, son of Petar, a doctor, served a compulsory military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. This document speaks for itself. Let's not repeat what is in the document. I want to ask you something about the document. This is the war deployment. What for you is the -- the wartime assignment, rather?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every conscript, every person who served military service becomes a member of the reserve military strength and then he is given a war assignment in accordance with the replenishment plan of army units. So this is a procedure based on the replenishment plan, which is obtained from the higher organs in the army. So this is a usual, customary procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the war assignment for, so to say, politicians or officials in the administration, what was the practice prior to 1992 and after 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the elections, if a military conscript is given a position in the civilian authorities, then he is assigned -- he is given the war assignment as assigned to this position that he has in the civilian structures, and that is then considered his war assignment for the purpose of wartime duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on what has this principle been designed? How come that a politician or a high official in the public life, how come that that person has a war assignment in his own position? Can you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence cannot contest the electoral will of citizens. So if somebody -- if a candidate in the elections has been elected and has thus been given a position in the structures of the civilian authorities, then this has to be confirmed in his war assignment. So the Ministry of Defence has to confirm that assignment by issuing a document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean for practical purposes? For example, when war breaks out.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That practically means for all intents and purposes that this is that person's war assignment. Have I understood your question well? I'm not sure that I have understood you well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, somebody is an official or was an official before the war broke out. For example, he was the president of the municipal assembly. What happens with that person during the war? What does that person do during the war? I suppose that would be his war assignment.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is issued a certificate about his work obligation, and that certificate says, for example, "Blagoje Simic has been given war assignment as the president of the Municipal Assembly of Samac, and for that purpose this is his war assignment."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does he do during the war?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He does whatever the president of the municipal assembly has to do according to the statute and other enactments of that municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge on how these issues were dealt with in another entity of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The issues were dealt with in an identical way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, could we have now Exhibit D57/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, this document speaks for itself. You yourself signed it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic, tell me, the term of work obligation, the notion of work obligation in very brief outlines -- we will go back to that in the course of the day today, but in introduction -- by way of introduction, can you tell us what is work obligation.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law on defence which draws from the constitution defines the rights of natural and legal persons. When natural persons are concerned, that is, citizens, they have the obligation to carry out military obligation, work obligation, that they have to be members of the civilian protection and they have to do the obligation and intelligence. And this is a legal obligation, and every citizen has -- every able-bodied citizen has to have work obligation. When I say "able-bodied," that's 15 [Realtime transcript read in error "50"] to 60 years of age for men and 15 to 50 for women, but -- women with small children and pregnant women do not have to have that obligation if a child is under 10 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- Deal with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Page 33, is it the same -- line 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said in the transcript, it says that -- that able-bodied men between the ages of 50 to 60. That is what it says in the transcript. Can you please correct that or explain that. And please, Mr. Ninkovic, these are very important things you're saying. Every testimony is important, and we are going to have a problem with the quality of the transcript. Can you please slow down, be more relaxed. These are very important things.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you please tell us. This work obligation, which group of citizens did it apply to? Can you give us the age range. Just slowly.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work obligation applied to all the able-bodied citizens, both males and females. The only difference being that for men that obligation was for men between 15 and 65 years of age and for women, it was for women between the ages of 15 and 60. But it didn't apply to those women who were pregnant, women who had one child under the age of seven. So that is mothers with children -- and mothers with two children under the age of 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will continue after the break. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, thank you -- if Your Honours please, perhaps my learned friend Mr. Pantelic could clarify what the witness meant when he referred to the law on natural -- on this -- derives from the constitution? Which constitution? What is the source of this law? When was it created?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm going to explore that. But I will continue after we take our break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will take our break and continue our proceedings at 12.15 -- oh, I'm sorry. I said 20 minutes, at 12.05.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, before the break we spoke about the concept of the work obligation. In order to clarify that, please tell me the following: You have mentioned a legal framework that regulated that. Can you tell me how was this regulated by the regulations of the former Yugoslavia. You don't have to go into details. Just tell me whether that was the principle based on which this was organised.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law regulated this matter in the same way as it was regulated in the former Yugoslavia, an identical way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what you just explained to us was the principle of the work obligation as it existed in the Republika Srpska, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know whether in the other entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina -- I mean, the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina -- this was regulated in some other way?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was regulated in the same way; the same law applied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. As I've told you, we will come back to that and explore it in more detail. This was just as way of introduction. Another question in relation to that document. It just came to my mind. I see that it was adopted in 1993 and it covered the period from the 17th of April, 1992, retroactively. Can you explain this to us. What is the reason for that.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason is continuity, the continuity of the authorities concerned and the municipality. So it carries more weight that way. This does not only refer to one person. It shows the continuity of the authorities in the municipality and the higher organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the preamble of this document. What can you say about that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to the preamble in the sense of this decree that is being referred to here, this is a decree on introducing war production and services. There were some other documents of this kind, or rather, regulations of this kind. This decree is based on the law on defence. It has to do with the powers of the government as far as defence matters are concerned. So the government passed this decree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the year of this decree?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1993. The beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When a person went out for work obligation, did you pass such a decision once for all or did you have to do it each and every time? Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that there were several such decrees, and from time to time these documents had to be renewed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically, if this is from 4/93, on the basis of Official Gazette 4/93, what did that mean in practice? What was supposed to be done in practice?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meant that this kind of decision had to be renewed or issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what other purposes were these documents used for in practice? What could an individual do with this kind of a decision? What did an individual gain by this kind of document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document certifying that a person had a wartime assignment. So whoever had a document, a decision of this kind, had proof of his wartime assignment. That means that if the police were checking his documents at a particular checkpoint, this was proof that this person was entitled to unhindered movement; meaning that the person concerned was not evading his responsibilities from the field of defence. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, just for the purposes of the record, I think we should make it clear that the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And this series of questions all relate to D57/1, and that's the document that the witness has in front of him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, in practice, if you know, what would happen to people who when they were checked by the police or the military police did not have this kind of decision or military ID, that military booklet? This is a fact that you are aware of and perhaps you can tell us more about this.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to explain. A citizen who is of military age had to have a document whereby he would prove that he was engaged in some defence structure. As for the members of the military, that is a military booklet. In it there is the stamp of the unit to which that person belongs. Along with this military booklet, the said person could also have an ID, a pass issued by that unit. This pass would show how many days of leave this person may have been granted. A person who had a work obligation and who had his or her assignment in a company, in a government agency, had such a decision. As for members of the civil protection units denoting work obligation, a civilian protection booklet was required and a pass. For members of work obligation units, the required document was a pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. One more thing: Paragraph 5 of this decision, could you please give me a comment based on practice and on your personal experience.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that this decision is fully in accordance with the decree on checking persons, vehicles, and goods. That is a government decree which regulated this particular area; that is to say, regarding the movement of persons, or rather, checking the movement of persons, vehicles, and goods. That is to say, that this is a proper document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, since you worked in the Secretariat for National Defence, in the period before mid-April 1992, was such an obligation in force practically for all the officials from the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat this once again. Could you explain this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period from March, February, January, 1992, 1991. I'm talk about municipal officials. The subject of the wartime assignment of political officials, was that something that was present in Samac -- or rather, did this apply to the officials in Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood what you were saying, you have asked me whether this assignment actually was in force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look, there were multi-party elections in 1990, local elections; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Samac at that time, different officials were elected. The president of the municipality, vice-president, and president of the executive council, et cetera, et cetera. I'm talking about 1990 onwards. Right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Great. Further on, for all these persons who held certain positions, was there a principle of wartime assignment that applied to them, to officials belonging to the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now -- tell me now, the president of the municipality was Mato Nujic, right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The vice-president of the executive council was Izet Izetbegovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the conflicts broke out in April 1992 in Samac, what about these two persons and the members of the Muslim and Croat ethnic communities in Samac? I'm referring to these high officials. Did they report to their war assignment posts? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to where these municipal officials were? Did you know that then or did you find out later? Do you have any personal knowledge regarding this? Where were they over those few days?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out about that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you find out?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were armed. They were in their armed formations, the ones I talked about before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have a document D61/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document from 1993. As we know, we are going to move on to another subject that is not chronologically linked to what we've been discussing just now, but I'm interested in the following: Do you personally know that there were violations of certain legal regulations, that there was unauthorised cutting of wood, et cetera, by military units in the territory of the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us something about that particular subject matter, very briefly. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And I apologise to Mr. Pantelic for making this objection -- or interjection at this point but before he goes on to develop this particular topic, can we just return to an earlier portion of evidence. Did the -- the witness said -- sorry, Mr. Pantelic asked about members of the Muslim and Croat ethnic communities reporting to their war assignment posts, and the witness said, "No, they didn't report." I don't think Mr. Pantelic has clarified which particular war assignment post he is referring to. Is that one imposed by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina or the Republika Srpska or the Municipality of Bosanski Samac or the former Yugoslavia? The source of that obligation is not clear. And this witness presumably is in a position to tell us about that and perhaps it might be relevant for that to be clarified by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let us go back to the previous topic. Which wartime assignment are we referring to? In accordance with which laws before 1992? We talked about municipal officials there and their obligation to report in case of war at a particular place. Which regulations were then in force in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regulations of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether these regulations were practically accepted by the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we move to the over topic, Your Honour, now? Is it clear enough --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: That last question, if Your Honours please, the witness is talking about the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That is his answer. MR. DI FAZIO: That is his answer. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can move on, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 1993, Mr. Ninkovic, what is your personal knowledge about possible cases of unlawful behaviour by members of the military? Which unit was this and so on?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question requires a bit of time. You see, at that time a large number of military conscripts were engaged in the units of the army. Because of the priority of army needs defined by internal regulations in the field of priorities, the municipal authorities, the civilian authorities, did not have sufficient manpower to man all the different government agencies in the municipality, inspectorates, et cetera. An attempt was made to resolve this by employing women, elderly people, those who are not military conscripts. And these services did not have enough power to prevent the unlawful behaviour of members of the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait a minute. According to law, who is duty-bound to stop the illegal behaviour of the military? Is it civilian authorities or military authorities?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please concentrate on this letter. Do I understand this correctly? This is a person from the PIK Samac stating that the soldiers are walking around and behaving --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down. He is overlapping all questions, and it is impossible to follow two speakers at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. There is a problem with the way you are overlapping the witness's answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour. Thank you. I do apologise. I do apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is very simple: Did you have any knowledge about this specific letter? You see it there. You see who it was sent to.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge about certain cases of unlawful behaviour of members of military units in the territory of the municipality of Samac and -- or rather, just Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which period? Which years? When did you have such information?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the unlawful cutting of wood --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, different ones. Different ones. Not only that.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This went on throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you know about the behaviour of the military or possible incidents related to looting in the municipality of Odzak?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over there the command of the 1st Krajina Corps, or rather, its commander, General Talic, introduced military administration, military rule.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll get to that. I'm asking you about very simple things. Did you personally have any knowledge about the fact that the members of the military were engaged in looting, unlawful behaviour in the territory of the municipality of Odzak in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ninkovic. Let us go on. We'll go back to these topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit D62/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take a look at this document. It has two pages. Could you familiarise yourself with it. Are you aware of this document otherwise?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I've had a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what you can about it.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian or municipal authorities had a problem because of the unlawful behaviour of members of the military. Therefore, they requested from the commands of military units to take measures in order to prevent such behaviour, because the municipal authorities are not in charge of prosecuting members of the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Ninkovic. Look at the document itself. Look at paragraph - one, two, three - after paragraph 4, something is typed out in capital letters. What does it say there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Serb army is looting Serb property."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you read the paragraph below that paragraph. Do you have any personal knowledge about such things occurring in the territory of the municipality as referred to in paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this pertain to?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it says here, and on the basis of my own knowledge, there were lootings, robberies, individual cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By who?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now the Exhibit D77/1 and then D78/1, 78A, B, C. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to skim through these documents very briefly, without any extensive explanations, because we're going to go back to this later. We just need you to explain the mechanism involving work obligation, which authority addressed who, and which way, what this looked like. And in order to speed things up, these are four documents.
