You can look at all four of them and give us a comment with regard to the entire lot, or if you think it is necessary for you to comment upon them individually, please do. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, we've got a minor problem here in the Prosecution in that we're missing this particular document. We'll rectify it. But I wonder if I might just see the document, please, before it's given to the witness. I do apologise for this. The English, please. Oh, if the English -- the ter documents are not going to be produced, maybe we could borrow them for the time being and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, you mean just to look at them from the registry -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Just so I can follow the evidence, if Your Honours please. I'd be grateful for that assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to assist our colleagues from the Prosecution, document D77/1 is dated 7 June 1992, was signed by the Secretary for Economy. And this document D78A, B, and C are the documents dated 20th June 1992. So these are these three documents from the 20th of June. All right. Now, Mr. Ninkovic, please take a good look at it and then tell us briefly what was the basis for the work obligation. We can see here that these documents deal with the work assignment. Can you please explain this to us. Who requests what from whom and how does this work in practice? Just briefly, please, as an introduction, because we will later come back to this. Slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The relevant competent organs, such as, for example, Secretariat for Economy, based on their assessment of the need to engage workers, delivers a document, a request to the Secretariat for People's Defence, to assign to a certain company a person with a work obligation that is needed. So they would request a person by first and last name with certain qualifications and education in order for that company or an enterprise to be able to function normally. If the person requested is not serving in the military, then a decision would be issued assigning that person to a work assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this work obligation, did it represent a military obligation but in a different form? Let me just clarify this. For example, if a military conscript could be issued with call-up papers to join a military formation but also pursuant to law, that person could receive call-up papers to start performing their work obligation. Does that mean that there is one single military obligation in several forms? Is that your understanding? Can you please explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a defined obligation. If somebody receives call-up papers to report to their work obligation, then that person is duty-bound to report or else maybe sanction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of sanctions are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sanctions ranged from submitting a report on misdemeanour up to criminal charges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now that we've touched upon that topic, can you please tell me, what is your personal view of the following: In that particular field of military service, duty to respond, and so on, what punishment was set forth in the law in peacetime and in wartime?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One system existed in peacetime, in the sense of the level of the punishment. And this punishment was much greater in wartime because it was a special kind of time and people had to respond to the obligations that they had as part of their war assignments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. I was just waiting for the witness to finish. If he can give direct evidence about this issue, fine. But not his personal views, with respect. If Your Honours please, there's just another matter that arises from the evidence that is unclear. Mr. Pantelic asked at about lines 14 or 15 of the previous page, "If a military conscript issued with call-up papers, could that person also receive papers to start performing their work obligation? Does that mean that there is one single military obligation in several forms? Is that your understanding? Can you please explain this to us." And the witness said. "Yes, if the person receives the call-up papers, they're duty-bound to report." Now, what I understood Mr. Pantelic to be asking this witness is there some sort of global general obligation to perform some sort of duty? And that can be either military and/or work obligation. And the witness went on to say yes. Now, that's my understanding of the evidence. But if that needs to be clear -- you see, they're two different things. You can be called up for military service. You can be called up for work obligation. But Mr. Pantelic was putting to the witness that it's really one and the same thing, and I understood the witness to be saying, "Well, yes, yes, it is." Now, I'd like to be clear about that and I think the Chamber should be clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can clarify that with the witness. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've heard what it was about, so could you please clarify this term of a military obligation and the subgroups that come under that term. How was that regulated by law, especially by law in the Former Yugoslavia, meaning prior to April 1992, and how it was regulated in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in my testimony so far I have explained this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But please repeat.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. A citizen, an individual, is duty-bound to carry out his or her military obligation, work obligation, obligation to serve in civilian protection, also to participate in the monitoring and reporting service and in affairs that have to do with defence training. These are all different kinds of obligations that were established by law. Avoiding a military obligation or evading military obligation is considered a grave violation of law. But also evading work obligation or any other obligation is subject to sanctions. The law on defence clearly specified what sanctions were possible, whereas the Criminal Code of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, which was taken in full and adopted in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska, clearly spells out the qualification of what it meant to violate obligations that existed in various military matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These various kinds of military obligations, does this in fact mean wartime assignment?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us go back to my previous question before the Prosecutor asked for clarification. Please tell us this: Based on your professional knowledge, experience, you as a direct participant in these events, can you explain to the Trial Chamber what was the policy concerning punishments applied in peacetime as opposed to that applied in wartime.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can explain that. Since I worked in the agency that dealt with defence matters, and I worked there in the 1980s, meaning much before the war, a person that evaded and did not report to a military exercise, such a military conscript was subject to a misdemeanour report. This misdemeanour report was filed with the misdemeanour judge. I worked on these matters. In wartime, a military conscript that evades his or her military obligation - and this can be done in a number of ways - either by failing to respond to call-up papers or by deserting the army and so on, is subject to a criminal report, a criminal complaint that is filed with the military prosecutor. And I worked on these matters during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the punishments? What were they like in peacetime and in wartime?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is radical. Misdemeanours entailed a monetary fine, and on rare occasions with respect to a military conscript that was particularly insolent, there would be a one- or two-month sentence, prison sentence. During wartime, a person evading military obligation would be subject to a very grave punishment in the form of a prison sentence lasting from 10 to 15 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know regarding these matters in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the other entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law is the same. The Criminal Code is the same, both in the Federation and in Republika Srpska. It was taken over from the former Yugoslavia. As far as I know, it was not until last year or the year before last the high representative in Bosnia-Herzegovina initiated the adoption of a new Criminal Code in Bosnia and Herzegovina. That means that throughout the war and for a few years after the war the law in force was the same one, and that was the Criminal Code of the SFRY. As far as I know, the same is true for Croatia during war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the law applied in the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina in both entities throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Ms. Registrar, could we have a document, D92/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has several pages. Please take a look at it. Please tell me, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decree of the government of the Serbian Republic of BH, dated July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's a decree, but I assume that this is something else. This is a decision by another organ.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were referring to the basis based on which this decision was later passed.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the implementation of this decree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who passed this decree?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council of Bosanski Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please remember to pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It was too much for the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I do apologise again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can you tell us, Mr. Ninkovic, about these matters in the territory of Bosanski Samac municipality? This involves agricultural works. I am particularly interested in this: In wartime, how was this obligation set up? But prior to that, please tell me -- Samac, I assume, is an agricultural area with a lot of farmers.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I begin?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Samac municipality is flatlands, and a large amount of the territory is very fertile. Therefore, people are mostly involved in agriculture. There are seasonal works throughout the year, such as sowing in springtime, harvesting of wheat in July, or harvesting of autumn crops in autumn. These are works requiring significant manpower. The effort is to conduct the harvesting as quickly as possible due to weather, and everybody able to assist, the elderly, the young, women, are involved in this effort. This is a tradition with our people to get everybody involved in harvesting. There is a so-called custom called Moba where everybody gets involved in these works in order to complete them as soon as possible. Harvesting means securing food for winter, and that is a vital interest, especially in wartime, when a number of various food items can be lacking and their absence can mean a catastrophe for the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in wartime and in view of insufficient manpower, what kind of problems arise?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that these were works requiring massive participation, requiring significant number of workers. Mostly physical manual labour, and also other people needed are those that can operate the machinery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please take a look at the second page of this document. Could you please explain this term "militarily not engaged. People able to perform agricultural work," and this covers children, women, and others. Now, we are speaking specifically about Samac and the various work units that existed. Could you please explain this term, "The workers needed for autumn works, agricultural works." Who did this apply to. MR. DI FAZIO: If I actually could have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps we could have the article so that it's clearer for the purposes of the transcript and for us to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that I made the reference and -- MR. DI FAZIO: It was page, not article. So it might be different.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Article 3, I said. Maybe it did not get in the transcript. Yes, Article 3, my friend. Article 3, second page.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the war requires that people be engaged. The priorities to have: All military fit individuals serve in the military and in the police. That's a priority, and that is regulated by law. The remaining work force that has not been engaged in military structure should be engaged for these types of work. This mostly covers the elderly or those who for various reasons to not serve in the military. When I say "children," I'm referring to adolescents aged 15 and over. Those who are younger may not be used according to law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about non-employed women? And can you tell us who are the employed women.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The employed women are those who had a decision concerning their assignment to work in a administrative organ, enterprise, or a company. Unemployed women are the remaining ones, housewives and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So which ethnic groups did this decree apply to? Which ethnic groups participated in agricultural works of this nature?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to obligation, there is no distinguish -- it does not distinguish among various ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Samac in spring and autumn agricultural works, what ethnic groups participated in agricultural works?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of all ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last paragraph of Article 3 mentions mobilisation call-up. Can you please tell us briefly what that was.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please read this. Take a look at it, and we can continue after our break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- Our lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll continue the proceedings in the afternoon at 14.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.01 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll continue examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, before the break, we discussed Article 3 of the decree, that is, its paragraph 2. Kindly explain to the Chamber the principle of mobilisation of the able-bodied population which was not engaged in military units. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, perhaps we should have in the transcript the exhibit number, since we've resumed proceedings and that we're -- that Mr. Pantelic is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, this is Exhibit D92/1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please comment upon the principle of mobilisation calls and mobilisation of able-bodied people who were not members of any military unit.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat for the Economy was the municipal organ in charge of the economy within the framework of the executive council and it had all the necessary information through general managers of agricultural combines and other companies within the overall economy, and they informed them about the scope of work which needs to be done, and this was then expressed in figures, in places where these specific tasks had to be performed and when. Then these persons would be called. Those persons who were not involved in other defence structures, that is, the military, the police, these persons were called to perform work obligation from time to time for a limited duration of time. For example, during the harvest period. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I wonder if Mr. Pantelic would be so kind as to clarify -- and I suggest this would also be useful for the Trial Chamber -- whether the witness is in fact saying that this work obligation was in fact part of the defence structure and part of the defence obligations required of a citizen. He seems to be saying that where he says, "These persons would be called. Those persons who were not involved in other defence structures, that is, the military and the police," had to do work obligation. From the way you read it in English, it comes across that the work obligation was in itself a -- something that was considered to be part of the defence structure. I'd just like to know if -- if that is in fact the case; in other words, whether the people who were performing work obligation are involved in the defence of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ninkovic. If you could explain.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is exactly how it can be interpreted, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The process of calling or mobilising that particular part of the population, which organ was in charge of that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the period that is relevant to this decision or decree, and that is summer of 1992, then it would be the executive council, the staff of the civilian protection, the coordinator of work units, and call-up notices were received from the defence department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are talking about the municipal defence department of the Ministry of Defence; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Is this the 10th of September or ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that it was the 18th of September, but the decree was issued on the 31st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the government decree issued in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this went through the municipal office or department of the Ministry of Defence, these call-up notices.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you why these call-up notices went through that particular organ. If, for example, somebody did not want to observe this obligation of the work obligation and if there was no proof that that person indeed received the call-up notice, then there was no proof to instigate any proceedings against that person. It transpired as if that person had not received the call in the first place. So that was the customary technique of calling up people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe this is not within your scope of expertise, but could you please tell us whether these people were compensated for the work performed. And if they were compensated, how were they compensated?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this decree, those who performed work obligation were entitled to compensation, and it was envisaged that this compensation was either in money or in kind, in food, so in kind. We still have a custom amongst other people that when -- during the harvest, if somebody takes part in harvest, then a quantity of the crops would be given to that person in return, a certain percentage of the quantity. So this is a customary procedure, habit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how that -- what was the procedure in Samac in 1992.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that people who performed work obligation were given a certain quantity of food, flour, oil, lard, sugar, coffee, tinned food, anything that at the moment was even more necessary than money itself, because at that period of time the rate of inflation was rather high and the money was not of any particular value. It wasn't worth much and it was much better to receive food than money, than cash.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that during the period relevant to the indictment, 1992, 1993, all those on work obligation only received -- were paid in kind? Nobody was paid in cash?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not what I said. I said that payment was both, in kind, that is, in food. And to what extent that was up to the organs which were obliged to execute the payments. So either the companies or the executive councils. Those who asked for the work force. So the executive council, companies, agricultural combines, the mill. So it really depended on the possibilities and on the wish expressed by the person who was on work obligation, whether that person wanted money or food. And what was the ratio, I really can't tell you and I believe that there are documents in -- either in the municipality or in the combines who engaged those peoples, and from these documents you would be able to find out exactly the ratio of payment, whether in kind or in cash.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D112/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell us, Mr. Ninkovic, something about this document.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is again a customary procedure by way of which an administrative organ, in this case the executive council, appears before the office of defence in Samac and asks for somebody to be assigned to a certain work obligation. In this case, the person was born in 1941, so he can be said to be an elderly person. I know this person personally. His name is Nikola Mikanovic, and I know that his position was the chief accountant in the municipality, and that is that. It is a customary document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I am finished with this document. Could we have now Exhibit D114/1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please look at both pages of this document. Bearing in mind the stamp of the Secretariat for Defence on the first page, I suppose you can tell us something about this document.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this document. This document says that the executive council of Samac municipality looked at the problem of the transportation of those who were on work obligation, the transportation to the place where the work obligation was to be carried out, and it realised that this should be done in an organised manner and that for that transportation subjects to work obligation should not pay; that this should be provided free of charge, because this was of the general interest of the community. So people were supposed to be transported to work on time, that they shouldn't be late. That was very important because if people were late, then there could be disruptions to the work process. At that time, there was no -- there was a shortage of petrol, so people couldn't use their own private vehicles, so the transportation had to be organised and that was of vital importance for the maintenance of the level of production of various goods in the area of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, please tell me, at the time when this decree was passed and later on, can you tell me whether this functioned in the municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Yes. Now I'm going to examine some of the documents under the section 2. So could we have now Exhibit D3/2, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, just to inform you that this is still a document, not an exhibit. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: [Microphone not activated] Might I just briefly see the document, please. Thank you. And just for clarification -- sorry to interrupt -- I take it marked for identification only at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the registry said, yes. It was marked for identification only. MR. DI FAZIO: Right. Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, looking at this document, have you ever seen it before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain the term in the last part of this document, "the transfer of materiel and technical means." What is this notion? What does this mean, "materiel and technical means"?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the literature pertaining to the area of the military, very often you'll find the abbreviation MTS. That's the materiel and technical equipment. And this refers to military material of various sorts and types.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, perhaps before Mr. Pantelic leaves the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't, of course, read B/C/S, but I don't see any abbreviation MTS on the original. I see the words [B/C/S spoken] and some other words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is there no English translation? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, there is and it says "materiel and technical equipment." I don't see any abbreviation in the English either. I don't see any abbreviation in the original, I don't see any abbreviation in the English. The witness says, Oh, yes, this is a military document because it uses that abbreviation. So where is the abbreviation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The answer was: What is this notion? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Simply as that. In fact, there's no abbreviation itself, yes, in the document, but it's just explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The notion was explained in general, not in relation to that document. MR. DI FAZIO: I see. I misunderstood the evidence obviously. I thought the document -- the witness was talking about this document in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Di Fazio, he said -- the witness said, "In the literature pertaining to the area of military, very often you find the abbreviation." He didn't say it was in this particular document. MR. DI FAZIO: No. That's -- that's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could we have now Exhibit D4/2 ID, please -- document, not exhibit. Mr. Usher, is this a two-page document or -- yes. Oh, okay. So could you put in front of the witness both pages so he can -- I think the first one is the colour page and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What can you say about this document, Mr. Ninkovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a mobilisation document which elaborates procedures and measures starting from the issuing of mobilisation orders up to the transfer of that order, engaging a messenger, the call-up messengers, as they're called, in the mobilisation procedure, then it elaborates the mobilisation site. It is a park in this particular case. That is where they are going to meet. That is their meeting point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is exactly what I wanted to ask you. Do you have any personal knowledge about the beginning of the conflict, the 16th and 17th of April, whether some members of political parties were seen at this particular place?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document shows that the entire process of running mobilisation, that is to say, from the initial orders up to the actual mobilisation of mobilised manpower, all of this is led by the signatory, that is, the president of the SDA in Samac, Sulejman Tihic. This shows that this is a military organisation based on a political party. I testified about that this morning -- I mean, the first time I appeared here, I talked about checkpoints and things like that. So persons with weapons were seen around town, around the town of Samac, at several places. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, that evidence -- for you to make -- use that and evaluate that, you're going to have to know the basis on which this witness makes those assertions. The procedure has been he's -- the document is put in front of him and then he gives that evidence. The entire process of running mobilisation from the initial orders and so on -- and then he goes on to finish, "Persons with weapons were seen around the town of Samac at several places." Now, it's not clear to me whether that is a conclusion that he's basing on what he's read in this document or something that he has personal knowledge of. If he saw people at the park, he saw Sulejman Tihic running around with a gun and lots of other SDA men gathering in the park well, good, let's hear about it. But not conjecture based on the document -- or even worse, something you can't tell is conjecture or an assertion of fact. We just don't know what he's basing that on. It may be the witness can really help you out. He may have direct knowledge; in which case it should be made clear that he's talking about direct knowledge or whether he is speculating or extrapolating from this document as to what the situation must have been according to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Since he was not the author of the document. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, that's one reason, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, you mentioned here that you referred to it this morning, that you spoke of it this morning. However, let us clarify something. You said that you saw the unloading of some boxes in the park. But tell me, in terms of time, when did this happen, the boxes?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at what time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that an Opel came there. Could you give us some indication of time.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was the end of March, beginning of April. That's what I said during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That's what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to say something else in relation to this document, by your leave. According to the structure of this document, I can see that mobilisation instructions were used from the professional literature of the Yugoslav People's Army; that is to say, that somebody used those instructions as an outline for compiling this document. I worked on mobilisation affairs for several years, and I know these documents, these instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you personally have any knowledge? And if so, when did you acquire it and how? Directly or indirectly? Where were armed members of certain political parties seen? I'm primarily referring to the SDA and the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already testified here about checkpoints, checkpoints that were established. I testified about the occurrence by the Islamic community. Then I saw armed men by the Sava River facing Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us which period.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: March, April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were these armed groups by the Sava River? What formations were these, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They only could have been paramilitary formations of the Muslim forces, in view of the fact that at that time one could see members of the JNA because they had formation uniforms that were very well known, generally known. At that time the MUP still wore uniforms and the members of the National Guards Corps were crossing over from Croatia and they also had uniforms of the National Guards Corps, the ones I saw, that is. And I wasn't the only one who saw them. They were observed by a great many people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, this particular term that is used here, place of reporting, how do you explain that professionally speaking? In which case is this referred to?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This place of reporting means that when somebody was in a paramilitary formation and gets call-up papers, call-up papers can be in an envelope, as it says here -- then this person reports to this place that is mentioned here, namely, the park.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge? Not necessarily that you saw this personally. Maybe you heard about it. So tell us, what kind of knowledge do you have, if any, about the park in Samac when the conflict broke out, that a certain number of people were seen and what happened. And if you don't any knowledge about this, just say so.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have now Exhibit D11/2, please. I think it's an exhibit, because this is an extract from the Official Gazette number 8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decree, and the title is self-explanatory. As we can see, it was published on the 8th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that they cannot see a copy of this document and it is very hard to follow it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters say they don't have this document so you should be slow when reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put the document on the ELMO. Very fine print, but in order to facilitate matters, I'm going to give you a copy so that you can follow this and this other copy can remain on the ELMO. The print is very fine. All right. The question is the following: During your work as your department of the Ministry of Defence in Samac worked in Samac, did you apply this decree? Did you enforce it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But let me say that I was not head of that particular agency at the beginning of the war. When I became head of the department, that is when I started dealing with these particular matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain that now precisely, when you came to head that particular agency. This is a good opportunity to explain that.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By a decision of the Minister of Defence of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I was appointed head of the department of the Ministry of Defence on the 16th of July, 1992. That day is considered to be the day when this department of the Ministry of Defence was constituted. So from that day onwards it was a republic organ, not a municipal organ, as the Secretariat of Defence was before. On that day I started employing persons who would be employed in this particular agency. Rather, I gave my proposals to the minister. And it was at my proposal that on the 1st of September, the minister signed decisions -- four decisions on appointing employees who would be working together with me in this particular agency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was minister at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister of Defence was Bogdan Subotic, that is to say, a member of the government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So this person was appointed by the Assembly of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. From the moment when the Crisis Staff appointed you, if I'm not mistaken, this was in July 1992 -- did you start carrying out some preparations in terms of organisation as early as then and did then the decision of the Minister of Defence follow?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to explain. I worked on information, and sometime in the second half of June, as you say, the Crisis Staff appointed me. But this should be understood in the following way: The Crisis Staff made a proposal, because it is the minister who makes the actual appointments. So practically this was a proposal, a nomination. But from that period until the 16th of July, I dealt with information affairs, at least in part, and I was slowly taking over these jobs that I had been envisaged for, so this was a transition period, so to speak. After my actual appointment, for the first month or two my activity mainly focussed on military obligations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And within this department of the Ministry of Defence, or rather, this is a municipal department of the republic ministry, to be quite precise -- who was in charge of these particular duties related to work obligation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. This is a republic agency which has jurisdiction over the territory of the municipality. That is a precise definition of the position of the department of the Ministry of Defence. Sorry, what was your other question? I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of hierarchy, you are related to the Ministry of Defence, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is another clarification that is required there. There was a regional organ of the Ministry of the Interior that was the division of the Ministry of the Interior in Bijeljina, which covered a few municipalities in the region, namely, Zvornik, Bijeljina, Ugljevik, Popare, Brcko, Samac, and Modrica. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- Line 16, there was a regional organ of the Ministry of the Interior. It was the Ministry of Defence. That's what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just a -- it's a clarification, actually. There is an error in the transcript. Page 68, line 21. Instead of "Ministry of the Interior," it should -- the witness said, "The Ministry of Defence." Because the question was -- actually related to the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can clarify that. You referred to the Ministry of Defence not the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've been talking about the Ministry of Defence all the time. Just another moment, please, so that I can explain this hierarchy with the Ministry of Defence. So the Minister of Defence is the chief and then comes the head of the division, and then the head of the department. So the head of the department is at the lowest position within the Ministry of Defence. And orders for carrying out particular duties come from the Minister of Defence or from the head of division if he is entrusted by the minister to carry out particular duties and to entrust the departments to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the municipal department of Samac and then above that organ, what is the name of the next level up?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The division of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's seated where?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then above that is what?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister of Defence, Bogdan Subotic, headquartered in Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Samac Department of the Ministry of Defence, was the Crisis Staff of Samac municipality able to interfere in its work?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could they issue orders to the municipal department?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me: This decree dated 8th of June, 1992, I assume that it was enforced from the time it was passed onwards. Was it implemented?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm trying to say is that the secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence was Mr. Milos Bogdanovic, who at the time was the Secretary of National or People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now talking about the period when you were appointed head of the department in Samac, and that was in July, based on the decision from the ministry. And then you served from that time on. I would like you to explain here, in Article 1 of this decree we can see here now that the work obligation consists of various types of work. But could you give us, please, a better, closer interpretation of this concept of the work obligation.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall explain. As I've already said, the work obligation is an obligation that was established by the law on defence. This decree, as well as some other decrees that were adopted later -- rather, the work decree was further defined by this decree and other decrees. The work decree can be considered as permanent work obligation in various institutions, enterprises, and so on, if there is a document called the war organisation of work posts. This plan is proposed by the director of a company and adopted by the executive council of the municipality. This document describes various positions in that institution or enterprise, number of workers, qualifications needed to perform that work, and then once this document is adopted by the executive council, it can proceed to the implementation stage. At that point director of the institution or enterprise, based on this wartime organisational chart of positions, sends a request to the Ministry of Defence stipulating first and last name of employees, position held, and so on, and requiring that these persons be assigned to that work. If the required person is serving in the military, then the Ministry of Defence -- or rather, its department has to send a written request to the unit where the individual in question is serving his service, asking that he be released and reassigned to work obligation. This usually involves some key work positions, engineers of technology, doctors, and so on, who were considered indispensable and without whom a company or an institution could not function. If the person required is not serving in the army and has not received a different assignment, then the department of the ministry issues a different kind of a decision that is issued in three copies. One is issued to the company in question, one to the person in question, and one copy remains in the archives of the Ministry of Defence. These are permanent positions that can be equaled to regular employment, in terms of obligations, business hours, and so on. The other kind or the other form of performing work obligation are occasional or temporary kinds of work, such as harvesting, clean-up of damage caused by shelling during wartime, or work in the military, performing different tasks in the military. In this decree, it says that there can be various tasks that need to be performed in the military. However, these are occasional types of work on the as-needed basis. So only if the need arises. In this case, the remaining residents, citizens able to work that have previously not been assigned are thus assigned to some defence structures: Military police, permanent work obligation. A list of these persons is made up. There is a person known as coordinator or commander of that unit, and he is authorised to call up these individuals and say, for example, "The three of you or the five of you will go today and work at the municipal utility company clearing up the rubble made by -- caused by shelling, and so on, or you will go and work for the army."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, when a military unit requests a certain number of persons to work within that unit, then who is in charge? Who is responsible for those people performing their work obligation within the military?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander of that unit is responsible for those persons. The person requesting somebody to perform the work obligation, if that is somebody from the army, then the army is required to provide transportation from the place of residence of these persons with the work obligation to the unit or to the site where they're going to perform their work obligation. The person requesting these persons also has to provide food, accommodation, healthcare - meaning if somebody needs any medical assistance - and safety of persons performing work obligation. And this responsibility is the same as in the case of a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any victims in Samac within these work obligation units? Were any of these persons with work obligation wounded or became victims?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, some did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us any idea? Can you give us a number?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were two or three cases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any wounded?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps three or four, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there are any proceedings underway for compensation and who are parties to those proceedings?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war the wounded or the families of those who had been killed launched -- commenced proceedings in relevant courts in order to enforce their rights stemming from that: Compensation, damage, and so on. And as far as I know, there are several proceedings underway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder whether, Mr. Ninkovic, you could give us some idea with respect to these two or three cases that you mention, what type of work obligation were they involved in, if you know, the ones who were wounded or killed that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military unit requesting persons to perform work obligation is not required to state in which kind of jobs these people -- to which kind of jobs these people would be assigned. That decision is made by the commander of the unit, because nobody within the municipal government or within the ministry knows what are the work force requirements within that military unit. That is something that only the commander knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ninkovic. That's not really addressing my question. My question is: You mentioned that you -- as far as you know - this is line 4 on page 20 - you say there were two or three cases of people who were killed or wounded. My question is: What were they doing? Were they picking plums? Were they digging trenches? Were they -- you know, what were they actually doing at the time of the wounding or the death?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it means you don't even know the names of the victims or those wounded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The unit in which somebody got killed does not submit a report to anyone but the higher military organ, or rather, the command, the military command of the corps, because this is considered classified information. I learned about this subsequently. And as to the circumstances of somebody's death, I know nothing about that. Only an eyewitness could know this. I am somebody who works in the municipal administration downtown, and therefore I cannot know about something that happened 20 or 30 kilometres away on the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just one follow-up question: You did, however, mention that with respect to these two or three cases that you -- as far as you know about, that civil actions for damages were being brought by the families. So in terms of those civil actions, the claims presumably have to detail when and where and how these persons were killed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that it is so, because it is expected that evidence is presented to the court. In that case, the family of that person would have to address itself to the command -- military command, because when somebody is killed in the military, a record is usually made, a record of those who were killed and wounded. As to the circumstances of their death, that is described in the record of the unit. So perhaps commander of the platoon or of the company or somebody who was in the vicinity, who was an eyewitness, can create such a record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you learned of these cases subsequently. Did you perhaps then learn about the names of these people, and when was this subsequently?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard to define how much later it was. In that wider area, some 350 soldiers from the local military unit, the 2nd Posavina Brigade, were killed and approximately 80 civilians. There were a lot of units in that area from the 1st Krajina Corps, so there were frequent deaths, almost every day. Sometimes more people got killed on the same day. So it's difficult for me to pinpoint when exactly this was, but it must have been several months later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that proceedings were underway. Can you tell us who the defendant is. Who are the families suing?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know any names? Do you know somebody who is currently involved in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought the witness had said that he didn't know. He has been giving lengthy explanations about this, so -- he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To jog his memory, Your Honour. You never know. Maybe at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because in the evidence of the Prosecution, the names were given of the people who were wounded, of the people who were killed during work obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you can still try and remember. Can you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Because Your Honour, I believe that he -- well, personally, I forget also -- I forgot also, but I believe that he mentioned one of these -- maybe we shall come to that later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Isn't that so, Mr. Ninkovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will probably remember later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at Article 7. As far as I understand it, a person who is subject to work obligation can fall into one of the several categories. Can you please explain those categories to the Honourable Chamber.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I've already explained that, but I can maybe provide you with some more detail or repeat what I've already said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's what I was about to say. I was thinking that this question has already been answered when the witness was describing the part played by the military and different institutions who wanted personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the basic question is the following:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, can you please tell me whether essentially this work obligation was war assignment for that particular person.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the coordinator of the work obligation unit in 1992? Maybe we could first tackle the period from April until the moment when you became the chief of the department.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was appointed the chief of the department, then at that time the coordinator of the work obligation unit was Dzemal Kapetanovic, also known as Beka. Later on he was replaced by Nermin Hadzialijagic, also known as Nirva [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, how did he become the coordinator? Did he have any previous experience? Based on what procedure was he appointed to be the coordinator of that work obligation unit?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know about this gentleman is that he had worked for a number of years in the Secretariat for National Defence in Samac. And then when the Federal law on defence and the army changed, and when the military territorial organs -- or specifically, the department in Brcko were set up, then he was transferred to work there. Then he left that organ sometime in March of 1992, and he was without an assignment in the Secretariat for Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the second person, Mr. Hadzialijagic, I believe his name was.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he did before. All I know is that he was a footballer, an amateur footballer, not a professional.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me when did he become the coordinator?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was in late August or early September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did he stay in that position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was up to May or April 1993. I don't know for a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, when a military unit asks for a number of people to work in that unit, what would be the tasks and duties that they would ask these people for?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just give us a general idea.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are usually jobs related to logistics, either in a warehouse or in a kitchen, building of fortification facilities, and other tasks and duties which are at the time required.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would the commander address in order to ask for a certain number of people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, the Prosecution case is clear, and there are specific people who gave evidence as to what happened to them during work obligation, which was called forced labour at that time. And I thought that you would be asking for these specific people to get answers from this witness as to what actually happened. If you have any defence at all against those allegations. It doesn't help us to give us just a general picture -- a general system, what would happen, what might have happened. It isn't helping your case at all. This is not a defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because there are specific cases that the Prosecution referred to in the evidence, specific witnesses with names and times, and those are the answers you would be dealing with in the Defence case, not just a general picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. I will come to that when I will discuss with this witness one list, where the killed and wounded members of this working unit were mentioned. But prior to that, the Defence case is very clear. We have to establish the chain of command and who is, by commander's responsibility, responsible for these people. So that's the line which I have to establish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: At the material time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not just generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just but for this particular time, when this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, covered by the indictment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. That's my intention, of course. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, somewhat related to that matter that Your Honour raised, I wonder if the witness might clarify what fortification facilities are, whether in fact they might be trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've heard the question. You mentioned fortification facilities. What could those be?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a company, the name of which was Usce Bosne, the mouth of the Bosna River. And that company excavated pebbles from the river and they manufactured all sorts of concrete products. And that company also manufactured mobile concrete bunkers. And this was done according to the design of the army engineers. So when a bunker, for all intents and purposes, we can call that a bunker -- when that bunker is constructed and completed, it was transported to the place designated by the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question: The period of 1992/1993, this is the relevant period that we are talking about. When a commander of a military unit says, "I need 10 people to work in my unit," my question to you is very specific and direct: Who would that commander approach and how would people be selected to work in the military unit on the request of that commander?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander would address the coordinator or the commander of that work unit. He would then take the list of the work obligation unit and he would choose from that list those persons that he wanted to work in his unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the performance of work in the military unit, who is responsible for those people?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the commander of that military unit. Can I please give you an explanation? In the criminal law, in the chapter relative to the military obligation in the army, there is the responsibility of a commander who fails to protect his men, men who are in the unit at the time. According to the legislator, the commander is held responsible if it is established that he has failed to put in place measures to protect his men who are in the unit. This is a customary thing in our systems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that somebody from Samac who was in this -- in any of the military units is suing Republika Srpska for compensation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Could we have now Exhibit D12/2, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly. A question regarding this decision, which is not long. This is the decision on the functioning and protection of capacities in the conditions of the immediate threat of war in Republika Srpska, and it was issued in May of 1992. Can you please explain the role of the Secretariat for National Defence. Would that fall under the scope of economic activities during the war? If you can.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The role of the Secretariat is primarily to engage the work force. So the secretariats are in the position to provide work force. Or if somebody doesn't want to respond -- observe their work obligation, there are instruments to take them to court for failure to perform their duties and obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document that I would like to discuss with this witness is D19/2, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another short question: You already spoke about this decision. Is this the decree pursuant to which the municipal decision on temporary work during harvesting period was passed?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the government decree from July 1992, based on which the municipality issued its decision on the engagement of people during harvesting period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Article 5, paragraph 2 it says that compensation should be made. Was that the same thing that was applied in Samac? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now Exhibit D22 -- D22E and F/2. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm sorry, that slipped past me, the last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Pantelic asked: In Article 5, paragraph 2, it says that compensation should be made. "Was that the same thing that was applied in Samac? Just say yes or no." Answer: "Yes." And paragraph 5 says that -- well, it's not very clearly translated in the English -- that free harvesting shall be organised for families of soldiers of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina killed in action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the -- MR. DI FAZIO: It's a different situation from what Mr. Pantelic was discussing with the witness, is it not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I thought that was the compensation, the free harvesting of them -- for the families of the soldiers who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps I misunderstood. I'm grateful, Your Honour, for clarifying the matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's just for those who were killed. We don't know the names and -- yes. That was the answer. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry I raised the matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please look at the document D22E/2. What can you tell us about this document? First of all, have you ever seen it before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw it in the municipal assembly, that is, in the executive council of the municipal assembly. This is the payroll. And the only comment I could provide is on the title. That is the list of members of the work brigade. The brigade here is not the right term. The brigade is too big, and there were not enough people in this unit to call it a brigade, so this is just a clumsy expression in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in this particular case, the compensation was in cash. Do you know anything about that, whether this was really enforced?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the second document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the assignment to a very specific work obligation, to a very specific position in a company. This is a permanent work obligation for [redacted]

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I believe this is under seal, this -- I'm told that these documents are under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The two documents, E and F, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for a moment. Just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are still discussing them, yes. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please, D23/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. If somebody had work obligation at the municipality and if he were to be injured or killed, who would be liable?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal executive council. I was responsible for my staff who worked with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at this document. Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a payroll too. Do you know anything about it? Were people paid in that period? I see that it ends with the month of August.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a payroll of the technical staff that was in charge of the work obligation unit. The names, the number of days engaged --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see that, but do you have any personal knowledge as to whether people were actually paid these amounts?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Now we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just so clarify, your question on line 10 of page 32, the translation says, "If somebody had work obligation at the municipality, and if he were to be injured or killed, who would be liable?" I presume you mean in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, in the whole of the municipality. And also, are you talking as well about a person who is doing work obligation not for the military sector?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, my question was related to the employee or the person within the administrative organs of municipality, which is a staff of -- administrative staff, you know. It was not related to the whole territory and then without any -- any relations, whether he was engaging in military or in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So the words "at the municipality," you meant, as you say, a civil servant-type position?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But in order to clarify the transcript, I will repeat that question, to be absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it seems that we have understood each other, but the interpretation sounds different. Let me explain it now. If a civil servant in the municipal administration would, during the course of his work, get injured or killed due to the type of work carried out within the municipal administration, in that sense who would be liable from a material point of view or before a court of law?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The executive council, or rather, the government of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And just one other question on that note, Mr. Ninkovic. Who would be responsible for, let us say, persons who were selected outside the old-age pensioners' building in Bosanski Samac and, for example, were given the work obligation to fill sandbags and put them around the first floor -- or the ground floor of the municipal building? If somebody was injured in doing that type of work obligation, who would be responsible for the compensation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you correctly, this was work performed within civil protection, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I would presume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In such a situation it would be the municipality, because the civilian protection is at a lower level. However, the commander of the work unit is the person that is directly responsible at the moment when that particular work was chosen. So you cannot give someone this kind of work assignment if shells are falling. There has to be the right kind of assessment, that this kind of work can be carried out when it is safe. Although, in a war situation, nothing is ever safe. It is always possible for a shell to fall. I can tell you that many times I avoided death while I was driving my car in town or walking on foot. The wall of the building behind my back in my office was bullet riddled. If it were a stronger shell, perhaps it would have penetrated the wall and I wouldn't be sitting here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, now we've gone into a subject matter like two lawyers, five opinions. Civilian protection, if it is part of the system of total national defence, is there a responsibility of the state as such involved?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it exists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's leave that for a subsequent interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Mr. Ninkovic. My question is the following: Could a political party in 1991 in Bosnia-Herzegovina have been active in recruiting police officers, according to the laws that were then in force?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have now Exhibit D33/3, please. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I wonder if Mr. Pantelic could assist us or perhaps the witness as to where in the document we -- that there is talk of recruiting of police officers. I see a request for the Party of Democratic Action in Sarajevo sending to the executive boards a list of candidates. I don't see anything about recruiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And I'm wondering, because I don't think the answer was specific to that document of the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: No. We're left with the impression that this is a recruitment document. And all I can see is it's the SDA trying to fill candidates or put it candidates for entry into the police force. Now, it's a different thing from -- one is left with the impression that they are actively engaged in finding police officers for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The police force. MR. DI FAZIO: For the police force, rather than offering officers for the police force, which is a different thing altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will clarify that gladly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very gladly. Mr. Usher, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, I thought that I could speed things up, but the Prosecutor would like to have a bit more detail, so now let us be of assistance. First of all, tell me, according to the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991, who was in charge and how did the principle of recruitment for members of the police force evolve, if you know of course?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know absolutely. Because we cooperated with the MUP in this area, and these are similar institutions. You see, the MUP of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about 1991, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991. And please speak slower.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina has an announcement of vacancies at the secondary police school and at the police academy. This is published in the media, radio, television, et cetera. It is put on bulletin boards. It is advertised. So this opening is valid for a while, and then candidates are tested; that is to say, they have to meet certain health requirements and also their academic record is looked at. So this is a procedure that has nothing to do with political parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how do you explain this document, this last word down here, greetings -- I don't know, what is this down here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You're referring to which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: To D11/3, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what? I know the Serbian language, but this is something like an Arabic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
