utterances.text: Oh, Arabic. In these public announcements and advertisements, did it say that in 1991 in Bosnia-Herzegovina political parties could recruit their own people?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heaven forbid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what do you infer on the basis of such a document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the most flagrant possible way of interference of political parties in state matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about the Green Berets and the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are extremist groups of armed persons consisting of Muslims under the leadership of the SDA, the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit D33/3, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a technical document. We don't really need to dwell on it much longer. My question is very brief, so could your answer please be brief too. Tell me, engineer Jovo Krstic is mentioned here, who was in the military and now the Secretary for the Economy is asking for his services. Tell me, were there such requests that were put forth for persons who had work obligation and who belonged to all three ethnic communities? Of course, if they had a special profession.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, this is Samac 1992/1993. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have now, please, Exhibit D34/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Ninkovic, what is this document? Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a call-up document, very ordinary type, calling a military conscript to deal with some defence matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On page 2 of this letter, I see that the JNA is referred to. Could you explain, since this is a stamp of the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska in Cyrillic and the form is in the Latin alphabet, what is the reason for which the JNA is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was this form for call-up papers, and you can see that it has a number up here, 7, where the stamp is. So these are the call-up papers that were used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am trying to ask you whether you had printed forms from the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska at that time in the Cyrillic alphabet or was there some other reason why this was used?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have any printed call-up papers of Republika Srpska at that stage, so we used the forms that we had already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps whether members of the Secretariats of National Defence in the other entity of Bosnia-Herzegovina also used these forms?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have, please, Exhibit D -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps the witness or Mr. Pantelic could find out on what basis the witness can say whether other secretariats also used these forms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please explain that. Could you please explain that, Mr. Ninkovic. How come you know that such call-up papers were used by the other entity too? And if so, in which period?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, these are prescribed forms, you see. This is a form that is prescribed and the only possible form for such cases. I found out from my colleagues who worked in the Federation of BH on these matter that is they also used these call-up papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is very clear and brief. And they worked in Federation of backwards. Up here it says the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So let it be a municipality in the federation. I am simply interested in a very simple matter. In which period if these call-up papers were used, in which period did this occur? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was primarily at the beginning, at the beginning of the war, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the reason why it was so at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there weren't any other call-up papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Does that, my dear friend, satisfy your inquiry? MR. DI FAZIO: Very satisfied, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit -- thank you, Mr. Usher -- D57/3, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same again, Mr. Ninkovic, very briefly. The copy is poor, but this is a decision dated May 22, 1992. This document makes a reference to the document of Bosnia and Herzegovina on general mobilisation. My question is very brief: The department in Samac, did it also have to enforce this decision of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, number 40385/2?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 22nd of May, 1992 - that's the date here - the then-Secretariat for National Defence had to enforce this decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And within this document, there is a reference to an organ that is between the municipal and the one at the republic level. They are mentioning it as the district or region organ. Where was it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in Bijeljina. And later on it became a department of its own.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, thank you. I have a couple more documents which was previously -- yes. Could we have Exhibit D4/4, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know -- do you know the person that is signed here to the right as having received this -- this thing here?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is this person from?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was this person engaged in? What was this person's occupation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was a worker in one of the factories in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, why would he in January of 1992 sign for having received 20 kilogrammes of explosive and 12 metres of detonating fuse?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Could we have now Exhibit D5/4, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know a person signed here in the lower right corner as having allegedly received this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know Mr. Izetbegovic. I had contacts with him. I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what these abbreviations O4 and M160 mean.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are abbreviations for automatic rifles set, and M160 are bullets -- or number of bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And "O," what does "O" stand for?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stands for clip. A clip has 30 bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, is it time for the adjournment today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will wind up at this time and we will continue on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
